p14.text: Paper diorama: the Primepaw shell built as cardboard and paper cut-outs laid on one cream sheet, lit from the top left so each piece casts one shadow down and to the right. The rail, the sessions board, the capsule mats and the composer frame are cardboard: thick, with a darker cut edge along the bottom and the right. The chat column is a sheet of paper level with the sessions board, with the thread and the composer on a second sheet laid over the tabs. Sessions are paper strips, the workspace headers sage strips, the capsules cream plates on green mats with the time badge straddling the edge. The rail icons and the paw are solid-colour die-cut stickers, the active one ringed in gold; badges, dots, the pinwheel, the busy pill and the pet, a paper robot dog, peeking over the composer are stickers too. The composer has a mic disc beside the send disc: pressed, it latches flat and turns red, the hint gives way to a sound trace in red pen and the time by hand, and what you say lands in the box word by word; press it again or Esc to stop. Stickers are stuck flat, so they have a white cut border and no shadow. Boards run edge to edge with a 3px margin. The Advanced options switch is a thick-card pull-tab sliding in a slot cut into the paper, with on and off handwritten in the slot, YOLO is a rubber stamp, a faded black outline when off and red ink when on, and the effort levels and the picker checks follow the Kraft toggles: cardboard that stays pressed flat when on, terracotta for Max, a green sticker check on a picked row. The white paper (the chat sheet, the leaf, the rows and fields) carries the paper texture of the Factory Overseer workshop walls with its colour kept; cardboard is a flecked board; the workspace headers are paper strips in their workspace’s colour with the rows’ texture, their count and caret written in pen ink; an open session’s title bar and tab strip take the same paper colour as its workspace header, with unselected tabs a lighter cut of it; the prompt box stays plain. The rail icons, the Select button and every other button are cut-outs in their own colours carrying the same paper texture as the chat sheet and the session rows, not stickers. Sessions under a header are a plain list, straight and 4px apart; hovering one shows a three-dot menu mark at its far right. A working session carries a paper pinwheel in the robot’s place at its left: four coloured blades with folded tips on an ink pin, turning. A factory task goes through several sessions, so its sessions are filed together in a kraft folder: its tab is the factory sticker, the task key and title, the count by hand and a caret that folds it. Each session in it carries its stage as a small paper chip with the factory’s step glyph (Planning, Plan review, Implementation, Testing, Code review), in that order. A folded folder still shows the stage it is in, the pinwheel while that stage works and a red badge when one waits on you. Same live demo, same Night toggle.

p15.text: Dark mode: the same diorama after dark, opening in the night theme (the rail button flips it back to day). Boards go dark brown, paper warm charcoal, and every texture switches to its night tile. Identity colours on buttons are mixed down into the desk so white glyphs stay readable.

p16.text: The other screens, light on the left and dark on the right. Each is a live demo on the same materials: a cardboard rail with coloured thick-card tiles, one paper sheet for the content, paper pieces with the wall texture, thick-card buttons, sticker pills and rubber stamps inked on the paper. The rail carries Jarvis, Inbox, Sessions, Workspaces, Memory, the Knowledge base, Workflows, the Idea board, Kanban, Factory, PRs and Background jobs; Agents, Skills and MCP servers live in Settings.

p17.text: A session with its side panel open. A session opens under one 50px strip: the portrait of the agent at work with the status dot on its corner (red busy, amber needs attention, green idle), the real logo of the harness that runs it (Claude, Codex or Pi) on a sticker beside it, the title, the kanban task the session is linked to as a kraft tag with the board glyph and the task key, the sparkle and the VS Code icon, then one row of icon tabs with their counts (Todos, Terminal, Pull requests, Artifacts, Files, Git changes, Background tasks, Side chat), each opening its sheet in the side panel while the chat stays the main content, a hand-drawn Done box that strikes the title and marks the row, and delete and close. The branch tag rides in the composer bar beside the working folder and the YOLO stamp. The icon tabs open the panel, one sheet at a time above the side chat: the todos, a terminal printout, pull requests as index cards (state, comment count, a click opens GitHub), the file tree with the changed files dotted, the working tree’s changes, the background tasks. Artifacts are clipped to a cardboard clipboard: one tab per artifact, a version stepper, and Copy, Download and Ask on the side under the sheet. Each artifact also shows in the thread as a paper chip with a folded corner, which turns highlighter yellow while it is the one on the clipboard. A web page artifact is a white printout taped to the sheet, because it has its own design. The side chat is a legal pad: asides stay out of the session, the session keeps working meanwhile, and Put in chat carries an answer into the composer. With both open they stack, so you can read and ask at once. The left edge of the panel drags to resize. All the contents are fake.

p18.text: When the agent needs you, the turn stops and something on an amber mat waits for you. It holds still: the amber, the Needs you sticker and the badge on the session row are the signal. A tool approval is a permission slip in the thread with the command or diff, what it will do, and Allow once, Allow for this session or Deny. Questions wait in the dock above the composer as one card: the session agent’s portrait, implementer-agent has 3 questions, and Answer. Answer opens a sheet with a folder tab per question, labelled from the question with a tick once it has an answer. Each tab gives the problem in a few plain sentences, the question on one line, then the options: buttons, or checkboxes when you can pick more than one, each with a line of context under it and at most one Recommended sticker. Submit sends them all at once and says how many are left until then. The inbox shows the same card and sheet. Either way you can just write in the composer instead. Your choice is struck with a rubber stamp, the thread keeps a stub of it, and the agent carries on. YOLO now belongs to the session, skips slips but not questions, and turning it on approves a waiting slip. Try it: these two boards are one flow in ORB-272, and with YOLO off any message you send stops at an edit slip.

p19.text: Knowledge base: the book on the rail. The notes board is a file tree on one sheet of paper: nested folders and .md files with their git state. The note is a sheet of paper: type, title, description and tags on top, then blocks you can drag by the grip to move. Drag a list bullet to move an item, or drop it onto another item to nest it. Parent, related, links and backlinks sit in the margin. Graph is react-force-graph on cork: index cards strung with thread that you drag, zoom and click open. The second pair starts on setting up: pick a folder or clone a repo.

p20.text: Home, the page at /: you talk to one personal agent, Jarvis, and it starts the sessions. Jarvis tops the rail as a cream tile with its portrait, the paper robot dog’s face, badged with the threads waiting on you. Above the threads, the factories that are on: one strip each with the factory icon, the name, its state sticker, in flight over its cap by hand and a red badge for what waits on you; press one and it opens the factory’s page. Threads are paper strips, newest first, with the last thing said, the time and a badge when something waits on you; rename and archive are in each row’s menu. In a thread your words are kraft notes and Jarvis’s are set in Fraunces. Jarvis leaves three kinds of cards: a session card for every session it starts, with the workspace strip in the workspace’s colour, branch, model, a live status sticker and the session’s last line; a helper card, an index card folded to one line, for a read-only look into the code; and a decision line for every call Thread YOLO makes. A job ends on a finish report on the sage mat. The header has the title, how many sessions the thread started, and the Thread YOLO stamp, off by default, which says what it risks when you strike it. Everything is fake.

p21.text: The states: empty, a big prompt box where sending starts a thread; a session waiting on you, on the amber mat, next to one that failed; Jarvis asking which workspace with the same question card and sheet a session uses; and Thread YOLO on, which answers waiting prompts and writes each call down. Turn YOLO on in Bump Node to 22 to watch it answer the waiting session.

p23.text: Home before there is a main agent: the same form, as a card in the middle of the empty sheet, with the rail’s top tile an empty taped frame and the thread column waiting. Press Create with nothing typed and the rule under the name turns dashed red with “It needs a name” under it in red pen; with a name, the WELCOME stamp lands, the portrait drops onto the rail tile, and the sheet turns into the empty home page where the agent says hello in its own words. The second pair is that moment.

p24.text: Inbox: everything that needs you, on the tray tile right after Jarvis’s with the unread count as its sticker. The left board is conversations, one paper strip per request: a thread with Jarvis, else a factory task, else a session, with the source on a small chip, the newest line, the time, a blue dot while something is unread and a red sticker counting what needs an answer. Five small cards filter it: Needs answer, Reports, PRs, Factory, All. The sheet is the chosen conversation’s items in time order. A question sits on the amber mat with prompt 1’s options and is answered in place; under it, Ask about this is a short thread that stays attached to the question, your note on kraft and Jarvis’s answer in serif. An approval is the same slip as in the session. A finish report is a paper report on the sage mat, filed when a task is done: the factory sticker or Jarvis, the key and title with a DONE stamp; when it was completed and how long it took in all, every session’s time added up; the issue in the tracker and the task on its board as hand-written links, and the PR; the time of each session as the factory’s step chips joined by arrows; what was done; the questions asked along the way with the options given, the one picked marked, and who answered, You or an agent; the retro on three sticky notes, what went well, what went wrong and the action items to tick; and Dismiss, which files it with an Undo. A pull request that needs your review is a card on the amber mat with the PR chip, the branch, its size and checks, and the first line of its description; Approve stamps it here, Open the PR goes to GitHub. A factory task is a card with its state as a sticker: Blocked in red with the reason, Waiting on you, or Ready for you in Planning with a button to the Plan tab. Answered items fold to a stub and say who answered by hand: You, Jarvis (Thread YOLO), or You, through Jarvis. Each item has a read mark and Done, which files it with an Undo. The second pair has nothing left in it. The fourth opens on Reports. On the third, the push in Add CSV export gets allowed by Jarvis under Thread YOLO while you look: the stamp lands, the slip folds, the sticker and the rail count drop.

p25.text: Factory: every factory at a glance, on the factory tile after Kanban’s. One card per factory on the sheet: its name by hand, its board as a dashed link (primepaw issues →), a state sticker (Running green, Idle a plain paper label, Off a dashed ghost, Paused amber under the global pause) and the factory’s own switch. Under them five counts by hand with their words: in flight, waiting on you, Blocked, to plan, queued; zeros go faint, waiting on you is amber, Blocked red, and a card with either sits on the amber mat. Along the bottom the steps that are on, as small chips joined by arrows: Planning → Plan review → Implementation → Testing → Code review → Merge; a step that is off is a dashed ghost with only its icon. The header has New factory, which opens a short menu of the boards that have none, and Factory settings. Above the cards, Pause all factories is the slot switch with its consequence in one line by hand: nothing new starts, what is in flight finishes its step and waits. Nothing pulses. The second pair has no factories yet, and New factory is the way in. On the third every factory is paused. On the fourth PrimePaw has a Blocked task, with the reason in red and the way to it.

s5.text: Settings: agents, skills and MCP servers

p26.text: Button, the cut-out cat in a bow tie: Jarvis’s first character, picked from five cuts, cut from cream and kraft in 1.6px ink, and the try before the pet. Every board wore him until the paper creatures; the boards wear the robot dog now, and the other agents’ portraits stay drawn stickers in his style. This sheet lays out every piece he is cut into. The cut: the kraft patch over his right ear, bead eyes, blush, a red nose, the red bow, two paws to hold an edge, with the paper’s cut edge around him (a light rim by day, white at night). The portrait: the same face as a flat sticker with a white die-cut rim and no shadow, never pixel art, on the cream tile that topped every rail, as the first Meet your Main Agent photo, and at the head of the threads board. Over the composer he was 92px wide, in from the right, leaning 4 degrees on his paws; over the empty home’s greeting 84px. He is a cut-out, not an animation: he never blinks, bounces, pulses, changes face with a session’s state, or does anything when clicked, which is what the pet does instead. The drawing is Kraft’s Characters asset, jarvis.svg.

p27.text: Jarvis, the pet: three paper creatures drawn on Comfy Cloud, side by side, each in three cuts. The robot dog is the one every board wears: an angular sheet-white hound with pen-drawn panel lines, a kraft snout and chest plate, blue ear tips, gold-ringed eyes and a red collar, the first character through the primepaw-character skill’s options step. The puppy was the first character, and the cat, a round-faced tabby with a blue collar, the second; both wait in the portrait picker. Peeking: over the composer, paws hooked on the frame, a sprite atlas per character with a row per mood (idle, greet, celebrate, sad, error, ask) stepped like paper stop-motion; the buttons set all three and a click on one says hello. The sticker: each head as one round sticker at the sizes the boards use (the sticker, the rail tile, a thread portrait, a row). The standee: a sprite sheet each (pet/<id>-walk.png, <id>-walk.json and standee.js), six poses by four facings, every cell one drawing of the whole creature, the three walking one round of a factory floor and taking turns at the benches. The pictures are the canvas’s uploads of the pet/ files: a board cannot show a picture over 2 MiB that it names by a path, and the atlases are 2 to 3 MiB each. Qwen Image 2.1 drew the bases, faces and bodies and GPT Image 2.6 the moods, turnarounds and walks, through the primepaw-character skill in mockups/primepaw/.claude/skills/; pet/build.py slices them and pet/README.md lists every prompt, slot value and seed.

p28.text: Session top, three compact variations, asked for in a comment on the session board and then asked to be shorter (the first round, A to C, is canvas version 124). The same facts each time: the agent’s portrait with the status dot on its corner (red busy, amber needs attention, green idle), the real logo of the harness that runs the session (Claude, Codex or Pi, picked at creation) on a sticker beside it, the title with its sparkle and the VS Code icon, a Done toggle, the pull requests with their comment counts (a click opens GitHub), and the modules: Pull requests, Artifacts, Files, Git changes, Background tasks (the sub agents). The composer bar keeps the working folder and YOLO and gains the branch tag; the kanban task the session is linked to hangs after the title as a kraft tag with the board glyph and the task key. Logs is gone. D: one strip, the title and one row of icon tabs on a 48px line (Todos and Terminal among the modules, no view tabs), the PR titles on a slip under the PR tab. E: two thin lines, a small DONE stamp, the PR numbers as chips in the composer. F: one line with the PR as a kraft tag, the modules and the Done sticker on a spine at the sheet’s edge. Click a Done control to toggle it. D was chosen and is the session board’s header now (top.py).

p30.text: The factory page: one factory, reached from the factories list on Home or a card on the Factory list, in five views on one row of card buttons under the head: Overview, Factory view, Plan view, Kanban view, Settings. The head has Factory as a crumb, the name by hand, the state sticker, the board as a dashed link, the curator’s line, and the factory’s own switch. Overview: four count cards, in flight over the cap with one paper slot per place (green taken, amber waiting), waiting on you, Blocked and merged; press waiting on you and the row becomes the inbox’s strips on a board with the ticket’s session beside them, the same strip, notes, capsules and composer a session has, only the tickets that need you; press Blocked and the inbox’s own Blocked items appear, with Done once it is unblocked; press merged and the list of merged tickets with their PR chips. Under the cards the Factory ledger, every event with its day, a kind on a chip (Curator woke, Curator decision, Gate refused, Daily digest sent), the words and a dashed link to the session, with a filter by kind; and the Tasks, every task in the factory with its key on a kraft tag, agent and step, a state sticker, filtered by state and paged six at a time. Factory view: the tickets under To do on a board at the left and the floor at the right, a placeholder for the animated one: a paper room per step with a kraft roof, the agents’ faces at work holding their ticket on a tag, a Blocked ticket parked with its red sticker, the belt in and out with the queued crates, on grass, sand or snow. Plan view: the tickets to plan on the left, the planner’s session on the right with Planning done, Planning done implement later, and Close task above the composer. Kanban view: the Board page’s cork and sticky notes with two places to drop a note above it, Into the factory and To planning; a dropped note is queued or sent to planning and says so by hand on its corner. Settings: the Agent page’s sheets. Name, Description, Main goal, the curator agent as radio rows with New curator agent beside them, Ticket sizing guidance, the Ready label with its tag; the six steps each with a switch, an icon to pick, a label on a dashed line, Kanban status, agent, least and most instances, room and floor; Biome; Trust profile; and the three numbers, fix rounds before Blocked, new tasks per wake, the factory’s cap. Save settings in the head. Everything is fake and nothing pulses.

p31.text: Compacting: the press, picked from three ideas (the fold and the push were dropped). What a session shows while the agent compacts a long chat, stepped like paper stop-motion and never pulsing: the earlier turns go into a flower press as slips; a frame at a time the wing nuts turn, the top board steps down and the slips flatten, their words squashed with them. The robot dog rides the board down and says Compacting in a paper speech bubble (a scissor-cut sticker with a white edge, its dots stepping one at a time). The dial on the board reads the context used, a kraft frame round a cream face with three cut-paper zones, ink ticks and a red paper needle on a brass split pin, and steps from 184k down to 42k of 200k; the composer’s own gauge reads what is left, so it fills back toward F. Done, a COMPACTED stamp lands, the bubble says Compacted with the saving, the dog cheers, and a taped summary card takes the turns’ place. It plays when the board opens and again from Play again; under reduced motion it shows the last frame.

p32.text: Jarvis on a pedestal, on every board without a composer to sit on: where a board has one (the shell, a session, Home) the pet peeks over the composer as before; everywhere else it stands on a little kraft plinth at the lower right, its paws hooked over the plinth’s top edge the way they hook over the composer, so the peeking cut and every mood row still play: idle, the board’s own mood (asking while a question waits, dizzy on a failure, a hello when a session opens), a hello when you click it, a cheer when you send, a droop if you close the card on a draft. Drag it or its plinth left or right along the bottom; from the plinth the arrow keys move it too. A click opens a prompt card above its head, the composer’s card made small, on whichever side has room; Send starts a session with Jarvis, the main agent, and a taped slip names it. The character sheets and the design studies leave it off.

p33.text: Idea board: the bulb on the rail, the one tile in sticky-note yellow with its glyph in ink. The Board page’s cork and sticky notes, opened up: no columns, each note pinned wherever you left it with a red tack and its own slight tilt. Drag a note anywhere; the one you touch comes to the top. Click a note and it turns into the markdown you wrote, in the same hand, with five colours and a bin under it. Escape, ⌘↵ or a click away pins it back, rendered: headings, bullet and numbered lists, todos you tick on the note itself, quotes, a rule, bold, italic, strike, code and links. New note puts an empty one in the first free spot and opens it; a double-click on the cork puts one where you clicked. A note left empty comes down by itself, and one you throw away comes back with Undo in the head. With a note focused, Enter writes on it and the arrow keys move it. Everything is fake and nothing pulses.

p34.text: Loading: Jarvis fetches, the one picked from three ways (the blank cards ruled in pencil and the one big pinwheel were dropped). It is what the Workspaces page shows while it fetches its list, and every other page takes the same state. The rail, the title, Find and New workspace are there from the first frame and the sheet under them is empty but for Jarvis: he is off his plinth, where a small card says out fetching, and at a kraft file box on a ledge. His standing cut steps between two frames of work, the index cards in the box lift one at a time, and a scissor-cut paper bubble says Fetching your workspaces in pen, its dots stepping. The box wears the page’s name on its label; that label and the noun in the bubble are all that change from page to page. When the list lands the scene goes in a frame, the cards come a frame apart from the top, the count takes its place under the title, and Jarvis is back on the plinth, cheering, with Got them in a small bubble. This board rests in the loading state so it can be looked at: Let it load lands the list and Load again goes back. The Workspaces board above plays it once when it opens. Only stepped frames move, nothing pulses, and under reduced motion it is a still.

p35.text: Settings: Agents, Skills and MCP servers are off the rail and live in Settings. On these five boards, the two lists, the two edit pages and the MCP timetable, no tile of their own is on the rail, and the Settings gear at its foot is the pressed one. The pages themselves are as they were. There is no board for the Settings page itself yet.

p36.text: Artifacts: the clipboard tile on the rail, after the Knowledge base. What you pin in a session’s artifacts sidebar shows up here, on a cork board, newest first, each a card with a red tack through it and its own slight tilt. Markdown, web pages and images show a thumbnail, the real thing made small in a window: a document in the app’s own type, a web page as a white printout under the browser’s bar, an image as it is. Anything else, code, a table or a PDF, has no preview: its kind is stamped on plain paper. Under the window are the name, the kind and size in Courier, and the session and workspace it came from by hand. Five small cards filter by kind, All, Markdown, HTML, Images, Other, each with its count, and Find looks at names, sessions and workspaces. A click opens the piece in a drawer at full size, with the session it was pinned from and Open the session, Copy and Download. Pull the tack, or press Unpin in the drawer, and it comes down; Undo in the head pins it back where it was. The page opens on the shared loading state: Jarvis at the file box, labelled ARTIFACTS, on the cork, and the pieces pinned up a frame apart when the list lands. In the session, the pin is a pushpin drawn in pen beside the artifact’s versions: faint with Pin by hand until pressed, then red with Pinned, the kind line says pinned to Artifacts and the artifact’s tab carries a small tack.

p22.text: Setting up: the checklist a new install opens on, six steps on one sheet with a tick box each, the open one unfolded. Meet your Main Agent is the only step that has to be done before Open Primepaw works. It is a form on the paper: the name on a ruled line with Jarvis pencilled in as the placeholder, three portrait stickers, the characters’ faces, taped on like photos with the picked one ringed in pen, and the model, which is the global default until the pull-tab says otherwise and then a provider and a model from torn-paper pickers. One line says what the agent is for: it starts work for you and never edits code itself. Create with no name writes “It needs a name” in red pen; with one, a WELCOME stamp lands and the step folds to done. The second pair restored a backup, so the step is already ticked: Jarvis came with your backup. Choose a backup on the first pair does the same.
